correctness.rationale: In update-order coordinates the exact sweep is T=−(D+L)^−1 U. In its characteristic numerator det(λ(D+L)+U), the nontrivial permutations are edge matchings and the two fully directed cycles. Each matched edge contributes −λw_i²; the only order-sensitive terms are −Pλ^a and −Pλ^(n−a). Comparing the matching terms with λ^(n/2) det(√λD−W) gives the characteristic identity and reversal invariance. Positive definiteness gives 0<r<1 for the normalized weighted adjacency. On [r²,1], det(√λD−W) increases strictly from 0 to det(A)>0 by its real normalized eigenvalue factors, whereas P(λ^m+λ^(−m)−2) decreases strictly to 0 and starts positive since odd n gives m=|a−n/2|>0. There is exactly one root in (r²,1). The full sweep strictly contracts in the A-norm: equality throughout the coordinate projections would fix every coordinate gradient and thus the zero error alone. T is entrywise nonnegative by the finite triangular inverse expansion, so its spectral radius is itself a real nonnegative eigenvalue. Since the scalar root is an eigenvalue, a larger Perron eigenvalue would be a second root before 1. Increasing m increases the scalar right-hand side at fixed λ and moves the crossing strictly right, proving exactly the two balanced optimizer classes. Cutting the circular rank word at its minimum leaves a permutation of n−1 ranks with a−1 internal ascents, with n choices of cut location; Eulerian symmetry gives the stated count. The homogeneous five-cycle has five one-edge and five two-edge matchings, recovering both stated polynomials from the identity. The supplied verifier was inspected but not executed; the all-parameter result does not rely on its finite spectra.
